# Manage vendor renewals and orderly offboarding

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before a vendor contract renews, changes scope or ends. An approved renew, replace or exit decision with reconciled access, data, billing and residual obligations.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Compile the contract and operating evidence

agent-runnable


Collect the agreement, notice terms, usage, spending, support history, data access and business dependencies. Verify the vendor owner and identify commitments extending beyond the apparent subscription end date.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Assess renewal, replacement and exit alternatives

human · human approval required


The owner reviews value, risk, security and migration effort with relevant teams. Counsel confirms termination or data-handling constraints and approves any negotiation or notice strategy.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the transition and data plan

agent-runnable


List exports, replacement systems, integrations, credentials, user communication and financial changes. Test representative data portability before authorizing cancellation of a critical service.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Authorize the commercial decision and implementation

human · human approval required


The designated approvers finalize renewal terms or the permitted exit action. Authorized operators execute notices and account changes within scope while preserving required service continuity.

- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile completion and retained obligations

agent-runnable


Verify data receipt or deletion, revoked access, final invoices and active replacement services. Keep remaining support, retention or audit obligations assigned and retain evidence of the approved outcome.

- Verify: An approved renew, replace or exit decision with reconciled access, data, billing and residual obligations.
- Sources: [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
